one_line: A royal mint official of the Western Kshatrapas, overseeing the striking of portrait coins that carried rulers’ names and dates across western India’s trade routes.

appearance.face: Oval face with sharp nose, medium wheat complexion, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, focused almond-shaped eyes with slightly thick brows, default expression a calm, calculating gaze as if checking a freshly struck coin.
appearance.hair: Dark brown-black hair, straight and cut to just below the ears, combed back from the forehead; he wears a soft, rounded cloth cap in muted maroon, fitting snugly and banded with a narrow beige strip at the base.
appearance.costume: A long-sleeved, knee-length cotton tunic (kurta-style) in soft off-white with a subtle vertical weave, side slits at the hip, and a simple round neck with a short slit and two cloth ties, worn over a wrapped lower garment: a light grey-beige dhoti-style cloth, pleated in front and wrapped firmly around the waist to mid-calf; over his shoulders sits a light, narrow shawl in muted indigo with a thin maroon border, draped from left shoulder across the chest and around the back, leaving both arms free; he has a plain brown leather belt around the waist holding small pouches, simple dark brown leather sandals with toe loops, a single narrow copper bangle on the right wrist, and small, plain silver stud earrings.
appearance.signature: A sturdy bronze coin die and hammer set: a short, thick cylindrical die with an engraved ruler’s bust on its face, held in his left hand, and a medium-length wooden-handled hammer with a dark, iron head in his right, plus a gleaming silver coin blank resting on a small stone anvil at his side.

ref_desc: The Western Kshatrapa mint-master is a lean man in his early 30s with wheat complexion, short beard, ear-length dark hair under a maroon cloth cap, wearing an off-white tunic, grey-beige dhoti, indigo shawl and brown belt, carrying a bronze coin die, hammer and silver blank.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a Western Kshatrapa mint-master: a lean man in his early 30s with medium wheat complexion, oval face, sharp nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, and focused almond-shaped eyes; his straight dark brown-black hair is cut to just below the ears and combed back, topped by a snug, soft maroon cloth cap with a narrow beige band. He wears a modest, long-sleeved off-white cotton tunic to the knees with subtle vertical weave, side slits at the hips, a simple round neck with a short slit and two ties, over a light grey-beige dhoti-style wrapped lower garment pleated in front and reaching mid-calf, firmly secured at the waist. A light, narrow muted indigo shawl with a thin maroon border is draped from his left shoulder across the chest and around his back, leaving both arms free, and a plain brown leather belt with small pouches cinches his waist; he has simple dark brown leather sandals with toe loops, a single narrow copper bangle on his right wrist, and small plain silver stud earrings. In his left hand he holds a short, thick bronze coin die with an engraved ruler’s bust on its face, in his right a wooden-handled hammer with a dark iron head, and beside him on a small stone anvil rests a bright silver coin blank; show him in neutral, front, side, and back poses to clearly display his face, hair, cap, layered garments, belt, sandals, and minting tools with the palette of off-white, muted indigo, maroon, light grey-beige and dark brown.
